sections.h2: Where is the Stokes County Register of Deeds and when can I reach it?
sections.html:
The office is at 1014 Main Street in Danbury, ZIP 27016, and mail goes to P.O. Box 67. The listed numbers are (336) 593-2414 for the office and (336) 593-9360 for fax.

Stokes County Register of Deeds service windows
ServiceWeekday hours listed by the county
General office8:30 to 5:00
Recording documents8:30 to 4:45
Marriage applications8:30 to 4:30

Notice the recording window closes fifteen minutes before the office does. A deed handed over at ten to five will most likely wait for the next business day.

sections.h2: What does this office do in a home sale?
sections.html:
The register keeps, indexes and preserves the county's land and vital records. Three filings tend to appear in a Stokes County sale: the seller's deed, the buyer's deed of trust if there is a loan, and the release of the seller's old loan.

Stokes County itself is young compared to its neighbor. It was split off in 1789 from the eastern half of Surry County, which means a title chain for land near the line may run into Surry's books, and those go back to 1771.

sections.h2: Does a Stokes County deed need tax clearance first?
sections.html:
Yes. County Tax Administration states that a deed offered for recording must carry its certification that no delinquent tax is owed on the real property being transferred, citing G.S. 161-31.

So a parcel with a past-due bill cannot be recorded until it is paid. Tax Administration is in the same building at the same street address, which makes the errand short. Its listed hours are 8:30 to 5:00 on weekdays.

sections.h2: What fees apply to a Stokes County filing?
sections.html:
Rates come from statute and apply in every North Carolina county. A standard instrument costs $26.00 through page 15, then $4.00 for each additional page. A mortgage or deed of trust costs $64.00 through page 35 under the same extra-page rate. Recording a satisfaction costs nothing.

The state also adds $25.00 for a nonstandard document and $10.00 for each extra instrument inside one filing. The fee list is described as complete and exclusive, with payment due before filing, so the county cannot invent separate charges. The deed tax is a different matter: the seller pays $1.00 per $500.00 of value, or part thereof, at this counter.

sections.h2: How does recording protect people on either side of the deal?
sections.html:
G.S. 47-18 says a conveyance is ineffective against lien creditors and purchasers for value until registered in the county where the property lies, and priority follows the order of registration.

A buyer therefore wants the deed on record promptly. A seller gains too, because once the buyer's deed is on file, later claims against the buyer do not reach back to you. Keep a copy showing the recording date and time.

sections.h2: How are land contracts handled in Stokes County?
sections.html:
Under Chapter 47H, a seller-financed contract for a one to four family home must be recorded, or a memorandum of it, within five business days. The buyer can walk away until midnight of the third business day after signing.

  • Default notices need a cure date at least 30 days after service.
  • Late fees are capped at 4% and apply only to payments more than 15 days overdue.
  • The seller must actually hold title.

If you sold on a land contract years ago, check that the memorandum made it into the Danbury records.

sections.h2: What can a Stokes County seller do before recording day?
sections.html:
Work through this list with your closing attorney.

  • Confirm the parcel with the county GIS site and the tax website's property record card.
  • Obtain the tax certification from the office down the hall.
  • Work out the deed tax from the sale price using the $1.00 per $500.00 formula.
  • Check that any old mortgage has a recorded release.
  • Arrive before 4:45 on a weekday.

For title questions about an inherited or vacant house, speak with a North Carolina attorney, and call the register about document form.

sections.h2: Which other Stokes County offices share the Danbury address?
sections.html:
The Administration Building at 1014 Main Street houses more than one office a seller will visit. Tax Administration is there, along with Planning and Inspections at (336) 593-2444, and the Finance Department, whose mailing box is P.O. Box 20.

  • Planning and Inspections keeps weekday hours of 8:30 to 5:00 and asks that permit applications arrive by 4:30 in the afternoon to be processed the same day.
  • The Finance Department lists (336) 914-9188.
  • The Register of Deeds uses (336) 593-2414.

One trip to Danbury can therefore cover the tax certification, a permit question and the recording itself.

sections.h2: What planning documents should a Stokes County seller know about?
sections.html:
The planning page links the county's 2035 Vision Plan, titled Moving Together, along with planning board materials for meetings held during 2026. It also notes that a regional transportation organization based in Winston-Salem published a draft 2050 Metropolitan Transportation Plan for public comment through September 15, 2025.

None of that changes how a deed is recorded, but a buyer evaluating a rural parcel may ask what is planned nearby. Planning and Inspections can answer zoning and code enforcement questions at (336) 593-2444.

sections.h2: What if the owner has died before a Stokes County sale?
sections.html:
North Carolina allows a small estate to be handled by affidavit once 30 days have passed since death, when the personal property, less liens, does not exceed $20,000. A sole-heir surviving spouse can use a higher ceiling that stops at $30,000. The affidavit goes to the clerk of superior court in the county of domicile and lists a description of each tract of real property the decedent owned.

Estates above the limit follow a longer path through the clerk. In either case, the deed that eventually conveys the house is still recorded in Danbury and still needs the tax certification, so bring the court paperwork with you.

faqs.q: What are the Stokes County Register of Deeds recording hours?
faqs.a: The county lists recording from 8:30 to 4:45 on weekdays, with the general office open 8:30 to 5:00.

faqs.q: What is the mailing address for Stokes County deeds?
faqs.a: P.O. Box 67, Danbury, NC 27016. The street address is 1014 Main Street, Danbury.

faqs.q: Is a tax certification required for a Stokes County deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Tax Administration must certify that no delinquent tax is owed before the deed is submitted for recording.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed tax in Stokes County?
faqs.a: The seller pays it to the register before recording, at $1.00 for each $500.00 of value or fraction of that amount.

faqs.q: Does it cost anything to record a loan release in Stokes County?
faqs.a: No. State law sets no fee for recording a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust.
